deviations.what: Two of the original's three controller behaviours are now reproduced rather than wired to nothing. (a) breakpointChanged carries its own currentBreakpoint event parameter to the backend (t_arg ${$parameters>/currentBreakpoint}) and on_event enables the Toggle button exactly when it is 'S' - what _updateToggleButtonState does; the port therefore adds an enabled attribute to the Toggle Button, which the original sets from the controller. (b) handleToggleClick calls DynamicSideContent.toggle( ), which is driven directly through control_by_id ( DynamicSideContent / toggle ) since 2026-08-21. It was a bound showSideContent flipped in on_event until then, on the claim that showSideContent is the property toggle( ) writes - and that is the wrong way round, so the button changed nothing on screen. sap/ui/layout/DynamicSideContent.js shows toggle( ) leaving showSideContent alone while it is at its true default and swapping the private _MCVisible/_SCVisible pair instead; setShowSideContent, conversely, re-derives those flags through _setResizeData( S ) and ends with _MCVisible = true, so the flip could never reveal the side content on the one breakpoint where the button is enabled. An unlisted public method is callable through the wire (the denylist covers teardown, model/binding swaps, event-handler tampering and the render lifecycle), and toggle( ) takes no argument, so nothing can be lost in the cast. Residual, recorded 2026-08-23: _updateToggleButtonState has TWO call sites upstream - handleBreakpointChanged and onAfterRendering - and only the first is reproduced. DynamicSideContent fires breakpointChanged exactly once, in _setBreakpointFromWidth, and only when the new breakpoint differs from the previous one; on the first determination _currentBreakpoint is undefined, so the event never fires for the initial layout. An app opened at breakpoint S therefore renders with the Toggle button disabled - the one breakpoint where toggle( ) does anything - until the container crosses a breakpoint and comes back. There is no declarative substitute: the S breakpoint is the CONTAINER's (containerQuery=true, width < 720px), not a device media range, so the device> model cannot express it.

The width Slider's liveChange is reproduced roundtrip-free since 2026-08-05. The original's handleSliderChange delegates to updateControlWidth, whose body is var $DSCContainer = this.byId('sideContentContainer').$(); if (iValue) { $DSCContainer.width(iValue + '%'); } - i.e. it writes a CSS width straight onto the rendered DOM node, and sap.m.Page has no width property to bind. The `css` control method added upstream for this class of gap (pr/control-inline-style) does the same write from the wire: follow_up_action( control_by_id, sideContentContainer / css / width / ${$parameters>/value} + '%' ), the arg being a full UI5 expression (CAPABILITIES). The Slider keeps its value='100' literal and now resizes the page again. Residual, recorded 2026-08-23: the guard is NOT reproduced. sap.m.Slider.min defaults to 0, so the left stop is reachable; the original skips the write there and the container keeps its last width, while the port writes width: 0% and collapses it. A wire that writes a computed value has no way to express "write nothing" - the alternatives would either invent a value the original never shows or add a round-trip the rest of this port does not need.

The original's onBeforeRendering sets setVisible( !Device.system.phone ) on the width Slider and on the hint Text alike (the view's literal visible="getVisible()" is a sample quirk that resolves to nothing). Both are expressed over the framework's device> model as {= !${device>/system/phone} } - same truth value, different binding text (app 030/344 precedent). The two long body texts are shortened representative Lorem (not gate-compared, static).

The sample's own style.css is archived and injected since 2026-08-21. The view carries class="sapUiDSCExplored" and the rule behind it (.sapUiDSC.sapUiDSCExplored h1{font-size:2rem}) was missing entirely - a class name with nothing behind it, the same gap apps 122/124/133 had. style.css now sits in ui5/sap.ui.layout/DynamicSideContent/ (closing the AGENTS section 4 archive gap) and reaches the view through a core:HTML style leaf.
